name: Phragmites Adaptive Management Framework Small Grants (AAMP)
summary: Small grants to manage invasive non-native Phragmites in the US Great Lakes basin using priority management combinations, with grantees reporting monitoring and management data back to the adaptive management framework.

geography.label: U.S. Great Lakes basin and surrounding watersheds

amount.note: No funding cap; amounts outside the expected range are considered

reporting: Monitoring and seasonal management reports for each enrolled management unit, a semiannual financial report, and final reports and grant deliverables.

eligibility.rule: Projects run throughout the July 1, 2026–July 31, 2027 cycle
Each management unit is at least 10 meters wide
Use one or more of the 12 priority management combinations
Apply only one management combination to each management unit
No unlisted combinations, other invasives, $5,000+ equipment, or site restoration

documents: Project budget using the Appendix D template
Satellite map of each management unit
Landowner approval and required land use permits
Entity cost rate agreement, if it has a NICRA

status.quote: APPLICATIONS FOR AAMP FUNDING IS CURRENTLY OPEN UNTIL APRIL 15TH, 2026!

opens.quote: Proposal Period: Accepting application proposals March 11 - April 15, 2026

deadline.quote: APPLICATIONS FOR AAMP FUNDING IS CURRENTLY OPEN UNTIL APRIL 15TH, 2026!

pool.quote: A projected total budget of $105,000 will be available to applicants

applicant_types.quote: Eligible Applicants: U.S.-based state, Tribal, or local units of government, lake associations/watershed protection groups, non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations, universities/colleges, conservation groups

geography.quote: Geographic Scope: U.S. Great Lakes basin and surrounding watersheds

access.quote: You may view the 2026 request for proposals (RFP) and template for proposals below

window.quote: Proposal Period: Accepting application proposals March 11 - April 15, 2026

amount.quote: individual grants are generally expected to range from $5,000 to $30,000; there is no funding cap and amounts outside of the expected range will be considered

reporting.quote: Growing management report due for EACH enrolled MU. Note that management activities must conclude at least one month before monitoring in July. July 31, 2026 - Monitoring report 2 due for EACH enrolled MU; conclusion of grant activities. August 30, 2026 - Last submission of final reports and grant deliverables.

effort.quote: Proposals must be submitted electronically as a single PDF and must be received by the GLC no later than 5:00 p.m. ET on Wednesday, April 15, 2026.

eligibility.quote: Projects are required to take place at least during the cycle period of July 1, 2026 - July 31, 2027.
Management units must be a minimum of 10 meters wide to ensure all five monitoring quadrats fit within the area and to account for typical GPS device accuracy.
Management activities aligning with one or more of the 12 priority management combinations outlined in the Background.
Only a single management combination (one management action per biological phase) may be applied at a given management unit.

Implementation of management combinations not included in this RFP. • Non-incidental management of invasive plants other than non-native Phragmites. • Purchasing equipment (defined as single items costing $5,000 or greater). • Restoration of management sites post treatment.

after_award.quote: Grantee must follow protocols to collect and submit monitoring data in July 2026 and July 2027 as well as three management reports in between (due on November 1, 2026, April 1, 2027, and July 1, 2027).
Grantee and any supporting project staff responsible for data collection and/or submission must complete and pass the provided virtual PAMF training course (approximately 2-hour time commitment).

documents.quote: Proposals must use the budget template included as Appendix D to itemize the following project costs, as described:
Satellite map (or similar) of each management unit to be enrolled and managed.
Written documentation of landowner approval and any required land use permits.
Please include your entity's cost rate agreement with your proposal documents.
A signed acknowledgement is a required part of the application.
